notes: The original r9–r12 factKey list is absent from the retained context, so these keys are reconstructed for the planned topics. To prevent overlap, r9 tests default layer declaration rather than layer order, r10 tests utility property-count sorting, and r11 includes reference subpath resolution and standalone CLI compilation. Border and ring default colors share one card.

cards.statement: Tailwind's default import declares a components layer before a project adds component rules.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's declared layers include components alongside theme, base, and utilities.

cards.statement: Importing tailwindcss includes Preflight in Tailwind's base layer.
cards.explanation: The default Tailwind import brings in preflight.css under layer(base).

cards.statement: Tailwind's utilities.css import restores Preflight after a developer omits preflight.css.
cards.explanation: Preflight resides in its separate stylesheet; importing utilities.css supplies utilities.
cards.misconception: The utilities import also supplies the default reset.

cards.statement: Preflight retains a paragraph's browser-provided vertical margins in Tailwind's base styles.
cards.explanation: Preflight resets paragraph margins to zero.
cards.misconception: Paragraph spacing survives the default reset.

cards.statement: Preflight supplies the solid border style that Tailwind's border-width utilities use.
cards.explanation: Preflight sets border: 0 solid on its reset targets.

cards.statement: Preflight selects Tailwind's text-2xl token as the default font size for h1 headings.
cards.explanation: Preflight makes h1 font size and font weight inherit.
cards.misconception: Preflight assigns headings a default type-scale step.

cards.statement: Preflight preserves browser numbering on ordered lists in Tailwind's base styles.
cards.explanation: Preflight applies list-style: none to ordered lists.
cards.misconception: Ordered lists retain their browser numbering.

cards.statement: Preflight changes images and videos to block display in Tailwind's base styles.
cards.explanation: Preflight includes img and video in its display: block reset.

cards.statement: Preflight stretches a narrow image to its parent's width with a width: 100% declaration.
cards.explanation: Preflight constrains images with max-width: 100% rather than assigning that width.
cards.misconception: The responsive reset expands images to fill their parent.

cards.statement: Tailwind accepts @layer base rules for setting custom defaults on HTML elements.
cards.explanation: A rule such as @layer base { h1 { color: red; } } adds an element default.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4's active normal utilities override competing normal component-layer rules with more specific selectors.
cards.explanation: Tailwind puts utilities after components in its default layer order.

cards.statement: Preflight selects content-box as the default box-sizing value for its reset targets.
cards.explanation: Preflight sets box-sizing: border-box on its reset targets.
cards.misconception: Preflight preserves the browser's content-box sizing default.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 uses property count as a sorting criterion for custom @utility rules.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's sorting helps utilities with fewer properties override broader custom utilities.

cards.statement: A custom @utility tab-4 definition lets Tailwind generate focus:tab-4.
cards.explanation: Tailwind registers custom utilities with its existing variant API.

cards.statement: Tailwind inserts @utility definitions into its components layer alongside component styles.
cards.explanation: Tailwind inserts custom utilities into the utilities layer.
cards.misconception: Custom utilities use the component layer.

cards.statement: Tailwind accepts &::-webkit-scrollbar inside @utility to style the utility's scrollbar.
cards.explanation: Nesting supplies the extra selector in the generated custom utility.

cards.statement: With @theme { --tab-size-team: 8; }, @utility tab-* { tab-size: --value(--tab-size-*); } gives tab-team tab-size: 8.
cards.explanation: Tailwind resolves the team suffix against --tab-size-team.

cards.statement: @utility tabstop-* { tab-size: --value(integer); } accepts tabstop-[8] as a matching utility.
cards.explanation: Tailwind accepts tabstop-[8] when tabstop-* uses --value([integer]).
cards.misconception: A bare-value resolver also accepts bracketed arbitrary values.

cards.statement: Tailwind replaces an unresolved --value() declaration with the property's initial value.
cards.explanation: Tailwind omits declarations whose --value() calls fail to resolve.
cards.misconception: A failed value resolver emits a reset declaration.

cards.statement: For tab-2 with @theme { --tab-size-2: 8; }, Tailwind's --value(--tab-size-*, integer) picks the theme value.
cards.explanation: Tailwind tries --value() arguments in order and uses the first successful match.

cards.statement: Defining @utility shift-* also registers Tailwind's corresponding -shift-* classes.
cards.explanation: Tailwind uses a separate @utility -shift-* definition for the negative form.
cards.misconception: Positive functional definitions register their negative counterparts.

cards.statement: Tailwind's --modifier() reads the class segment before / in a functional utility.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's --modifier() resolves the modifier segment after /.
cards.misconception: The modifier resolver reads the base utility value.

cards.statement: Tailwind joins selectors when @apply reuses an existing utility inside a custom rule.
cards.explanation: Tailwind inserts utility declarations into the rule containing @apply.
cards.misconception: @apply shares rules through selector joining.

cards.statement: Tailwind applies @variant dark to declarations nested inside a custom CSS rule.
cards.explanation: The @variant block wraps those declarations in the chosen Tailwind condition.

cards.statement: Tailwind uses @reference to expose main-stylesheet definitions inside separately processed CSS Modules.
cards.explanation: @reference makes theme variables, custom utilities, and custom variants available to CSS Modules.

cards.statement: In a customized project, @reference 'tailwindcss' exposes app.css custom utilities.
cards.explanation: A customized project's separate stylesheets reference its main stylesheet to see its custom definitions.
cards.misconception: Referencing Tailwind itself includes application customizations.

cards.statement: Tailwind copies referenced stylesheet rules into component output when it processes @reference.
cards.explanation: @reference supplies definitions while omitting the referenced stylesheet's emitted styles.
cards.misconception: Reference imports duplicate the stylesheet's rules.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 starts its stylesheet through @import 'tailwindcss'.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's current entry stylesheet imports the framework using CSS @import.

cards.statement: Tailwind bundles local CSS @import files into the project's compiled stylesheet.
cards.explanation: Tailwind performs CSS import bundling during compilation.

cards.statement: Tailwind adds vendor prefixes while processing the project's custom CSS declarations.
cards.explanation: Vendor prefixing belongs to Tailwind's documented CSS build processing.

cards.statement: Tailwind's documented Lightning CSS nesting step preserves nested selector blocks in its output.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's Lightning CSS processing flattens nested CSS into ordinary selector rules.
cards.misconception: Tailwind leaves authored CSS nesting unchanged in its documented output.

cards.statement: Tailwind's Vite plugin supplies Tailwind compilation directly in Vite's pipeline.
cards.explanation: Vite's build configuration registers Tailwind's plugin to process the CSS entry stylesheet.

cards.statement: PostCSS itself expands Tailwind's @theme directives before the Tailwind plugin runs.
cards.explanation: Tailwind processing runs through the Tailwind plugin registered in the PostCSS configuration.
cards.misconception: PostCSS's core performs Tailwind-specific compilation.

cards.statement: Tailwind CLI provides a standalone executable that performs Tailwind compilation outside Node.js.
cards.explanation: The standalone Tailwind CLI executable runs independently of a Node.js installation.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 documents Sass as a supported preprocessing stage in its build workflow.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4's documented workflow is not designed for Sass, Less, or Stylus.
cards.misconception: Tailwind v4 retains a documented Sass preprocessing stage.

cards.statement: Tailwind resolves @reference '#app.css' through package.json's exports map.
cards.explanation: Tailwind resolves this subpath alias through the package.json imports map.
cards.misconception: Reference aliases use package exports rather than package imports.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 automatically discovers tailwind.config.js during compilation.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 loads a JavaScript configuration when CSS explicitly names it with @config.
cards.misconception: Legacy JavaScript configuration discovery remains automatic.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 gives CSS definitions precedence when legacy configuration values conflict.
cards.explanation: Tailwind merges CSS and legacy configuration where possible; conflicting CSS definitions take precedence.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 honors corePlugins, safelist, and separator in a JavaScript configuration.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 excludes corePlugins, safelist, and separator from supported JavaScript options.
cards.misconception: Legacy JavaScript options retain complete compatibility.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 loads a legacy JavaScript plugin through an @plugin directive.
cards.explanation: @plugin accepts a package name or local path for compatibility with JavaScript plugins.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 retains theme() as a deprecated compatibility function.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's theme() function remains available for legacy usage despite its deprecated status.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 exposes resolveConfig for resolving a legacy JavaScript theme.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 removes the resolveConfig function exported by v3.
cards.misconception: resolveConfig remains part of the v4 JavaScript API.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 preserves an untouched to-* stop when a dark:from-* utility changes a gradient.
cards.explanation: Changing a gradient stop through a v4 variant retains the other stop values.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 uses currentColor as the default color for borders and rings.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4's default border and ring colors follow currentColor.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 resets scale-150 when focus:transform-none becomes active.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 uses an individual scale property; focus:scale-none resets scale-150.
cards.misconception: transform-none resets utilities backed by individual transform properties.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4's space-y-* selector filters out children carrying a hidden attribute.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's v4 space-y-* selector matches direct children except the last, including hidden children.
cards.misconception: The space selector retains v3's hidden-child filter.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 puts divide-y-* separators on the bottom edge of preceding children.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's v4 divide-y-* utilities assign bottom borders to direct children except the last.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 honors legacy container.center and container.padding configuration options.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 removes the container utility's center and padding configuration options.
cards.misconception: The v3 container configuration remains active in v4.
